glossary.def: The pronunciation pattern of a later-learned language, shaped by transfer from the learner's first language's phonology.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 12]

glossary.def: A speaker's/signer's judgment about whether a form is possible in their language; an empirical observation used as data. Also called a grammaticality judgment.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: The subfield studying the physical sound waves of spoken language (no comparable light-wave subfield exists yet for signed languages).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: The moving (lower) articulator in a consonant — e.g., the lower lip or a part of the tongue (tip/blade/front/back/root) or the epiglottis.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: A modifier attached at an extra bar level — neither a specifier nor a complement (e.g., a modifying PP).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: Someone acquiring a language after childhood; adults differ from child learners in cognition, existing language knowledge, and motivation.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 12]

glossary.def: A bound morpheme that must attach to a base (prefix, suffix, circumfix, infix, or simultaneous affix).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: A plosive with a slow, fricated release (e.g., the start of jet); counts as a single phone.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: The convention year;month for a child's age (e.g., 2;6 = two years, six months).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 11]

glossary.def: The age at which someone begins learning a language; earlier onset is generally associated with more native-like attainment, especially for phonology/accent.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 12]

glossary.def: The thematic role of an animate participant that does something on purpose (e.g., 'The pirate sank the ship').
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: A synthetic type where words are built from many easily separated affixes, each with one consistent meaning (e.g., Japanese tabe-sase-rare-ta).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: One of the variant forms of a morpheme (e.g., English plural -s/-z/-ɪz/-(r)en/internal change/-∅).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: When one morpheme with a consistent meaning appears in different forms depending on its environment.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: One of the physical phones that realize a phoneme in a particular environment (e.g., [ɾ] and [tʰ] are allophones of English /t/).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 4]

glossary.def: Inferring language change by comparing speakers of different ages at one time (older vs. younger as a proxy for earlier vs. later).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 10]

glossary.def: A consonant with articulators far enough apart to give little/no frication. Central (e.g., yet, wet) vs. lateral, where air flows around the tongue sides (e.g., let).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: The property that, for most words, the pairing between a word's form and its meaning is conventional rather than inherent (e.g., 'pumpkin' vs. Nishnaabemwin 'kosmaan').
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: A phrase (usually a noun phrase) corresponding to a participant in the predicate's event.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: The set of arguments a predicate requires and the thematic roles it assigns; can be changed by operations like the passive.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: Using parts of the body to give a message physical reality — the movements/configurations that produce a linguistic signal (sound waves for speech, light waves for sign).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: Knowledge of how the articulators (mouth, tongue, lips; or hands, fingers, wrists) are used to produce the sounds or signs of a language.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: A puff of air on a plosive, transcribed [ʰ] (e.g., aspirated [tʰ] in 'atomic').
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 4]

glossary.def: An illocutionary act of putting forward a proposition as true (a statement).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 8]

glossary.def: The most common rule type: a phoneme changes to match a property of its environment (e.g., French sonorant devoicing; nasal-place assimilation; vowel nasalization).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 4]

glossary.def: The main, literal, 'surface' meaning of a sentence — the primary issue being conveyed; targeted by sentential negation ('it is not the case that…'). Often called truth-conditional meaning.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 8]

glossary.def: A functional verb carrying tense/aspect/mood (have, be, will, can); analyzed as the head T (tense).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: An early stage where babies practice producing the units of language; vocal babbling begins ~0;6 in hearing and deaf babies, and babies in signing environments babble on the hands (manual babbling).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 11]

glossary.def: Horizontal tongue position: front (beat), central (but), or back (boot). Do not confuse central (backness) with mid (height).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: The intermediate node (X') between the head (X) and the full phrase (XP) in X-bar structure.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: The unit an affix attaches to; can itself be simple or complex (library → librarian → librarianship).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: The order of subject, object, and verb in a neutral declarative clause. English is SVO; the most common type worldwide is SOV; all six orders are attested.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: Information that flows from the physical signal up to the brain during perception (the incoming acoustic/visual input).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 13]

glossary.def: A morpheme that must occur with other morphemes (all affixes, plus bound roots like -whelmed); shown with a hyphen on its attaching side.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: The property of an implicature that it can be explicitly denied or suspended without contradiction — distinguishing it from an entailment.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 8]

glossary.def: Repeated consonant-vowel syllables like [bababa] or [dadada] that emerge as babies gain articulatory control.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 11]

glossary.def: A change fully determined by the linguistic environment (not free social choice), which therefore does NOT count as a sociolinguistic variable.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 10]

glossary.def: Language change that speakers are consciously aware of, often spreading from higher-prestige speech (e.g., importing 'r-fulness' into NYC English).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 10]

glossary.def: Language change below conscious awareness, spreading through the vernacular.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 10]

glossary.def: The special register caregivers often use with infants (exaggerated prosody, simplified forms), which can support acquisition.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 11]

glossary.def: An affix attached around its base — part before and part after (e.g., Meskwaki ne-…-ena·n 'our').
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: A constituent containing a subject and a predicate; some clauses are embedded inside others, so not every clause is an independent sentence.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: The consonant(s) after the nucleus. A syllable with a coda is closed; without one, open. A syllable with no onset is onsetless.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: A term that is secretly derogatory only to those with in-group knowledge (e.g., 'Monday' used as a coded racial slur) — derogatory without necessarily causing offense to the unaware target.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: A phrase selected by (required by) a head, sitting close to it (e.g., the object NP that a verb selects).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: When two phones never occur in the same environment (non-overlapping). They may be allophones of the SAME phoneme (if phonetically similar) or of different phonemes.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 4]

glossary.def: A functional category (C) introducing an embedded clause (that, if, whether).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: A sentence containing a subordinate embedded clause (a clause inside a clause) — an instance of recursion.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: A sentence with two or more clauses joined by a coordinator (and, or, but).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: Building a word from two or more roots (e.g., blackboard, dog-tired); in English, compounds are stressed on their first member.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: Two sides of proficiency; learners often understand more than they can produce, and both improve as proficiency grows.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 12]

glossary.def: A phone made with a relatively narrow constriction somewhere in the vocal tract.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: A diagnostic showing that a string of words is a constituent: substitution/pro-form replacement, movement, it-cleft, stand-alone (fragment) answer, and (less reliably) coordination.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: A group of words that functions as a single unit in the structure of a sentence; identified with constituency tests.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: A question formed with a wh-word (who, what, where…), also called a wh-question; involves wh-movement to the front.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: The shared situation and common ground (what participants mutually take to be established) against which utterances are interpreted and update the conversation.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 8]

glossary.def: The class with continuous oral airflow: fricatives and approximants (sometimes trills).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: When two phones can occur in the same environment (overlapping distributions); proven by a single minimal pair. Contrastive phones belong to different phonemes.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 4]

glossary.def: An inference a listener draws from an utterance in context, beyond its literal meaning, by assuming the speaker is being cooperative; cancellable.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 8]

glossary.def: Grice's principle that, in conversation, participants generally cooperate toward the accepted purpose of the talk; the basis for calculating implicatures.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 8]

glossary.def: Joining two elements with a coordinator (and, or, but); also called conjunction. Coordinated elements are usually the same type of constituent.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: A large database collecting real examples of language use (books, newspapers, message boards, video, audio) used as a tool for making observations.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: A noun that can be counted and pluralized and take numerals/'many' (e.g., three cats).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 7]

glossary.def: Hidden, in-group prestige attached to a non-standard variety, indexing values like toughness or local solidarity.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 10]

glossary.def: A projection of C (complementizer); embedded clauses are CPs, and the landing site for moved auxiliaries (T-to-C) and wh-phrases.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: A window early in life during which language is acquired most readily and to native-like attainment; acquisition is harder afterward.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 11]

glossary.def: Using a trans person's former (pre-transition) name, whether accidentally or deliberately; a way names are used to enforce power.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: A clause type used to make a statement (true or false).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: Conscious, fact-like knowledge (e.g., explicitly knowing a grammar rule); one of two memory systems relevant to later language learning (Paradis).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 12]

glossary.def: What a linguistic expression points to in the world (more precisely, in our cognitive model of the world); written ⟦x⟧. The denotation of 'pencil' is the set of all pencils.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 7]

glossary.def: Morphology that changes the meaning or the lexical category of its base (e.g., -er turns the verb teach into the noun teacher).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: Harm in which a linguistic expression disparages people; expresses the utterer's condemnation of a referent.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: Describing expressions that disparage people. Offense (impact on hearers) and derogation (utterer's attitude) are distinct: an expression can be one, both, or neither.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: Describing what people actually do with their language, without judging it — the goal of scientific linguistics.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: A functional category (D) marking a noun phrase (the, a, this, my, 's-possessors); determiners are in complementary distribution with each other.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: A variety of a language associated with a region or group; note that everyone speaks a dialect and no dialect is linguistically better than another.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 10]

glossary.def: The older study of variation across regional dialects, producing dialect maps; early work was biased toward N.O.R.M. speakers (non-mobile older rural males).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 10]

glossary.def: A vowel that shifts from one quality to another within a single phone (e.g., the vowel in toy).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: The argument that (in English) appears after the verb; accusative case if a pronoun (me, us, them).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: The overall set of environments in which a given phone can occur.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 4]

glossary.def: The hand used more for daily tasks and one-handed signs; the other is the nondominant hand (often the location in two-handed signs).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: Evidence (e.g., from EEG) that the brain registers phonological contrasts very early in perceptual processing, before higher-level areas engage.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 13]

glossary.def: Placing one clause inside another; the outer clause is the matrix/main clause and the inner one is the embedded (subordinate) clause.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: Based on systematic observation of data as evidence for theories.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: A language with a shrinking community of speakers, at risk of falling out of use — often the legacy of colonial policies.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 9]

glossary.def: The process by which a set of linguistic features becomes recognized as a distinct, socially meaningful register or 'way of speaking' (e.g., Canadian 'eh').
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 10]

glossary.def: A relation where if sentence p is true, q is necessarily true. Tested with the contradiction test: negating an entailment while asserting the original yields a contradiction.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 7]

glossary.def: The surrounding context (usually the phone(s) immediately left and/or right) that determines which allophone of a phoneme is used.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 4]

glossary.def: The thematic role of an animate participant that perceives or undergoes a mental state (e.g., 'Pirates frighten me').
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: An expression used for emotional outbursts (e.g., damn). An expression can be both a vulgarity and an expletive.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: The default principle that a phoneme is pronounced as its matching default allophone in any environment not covered by a rule ('faithful' to the phoneme).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 4]

glossary.def: A language learned from the people around you in early childhood; a person may have more than one L1. (Contrast with L2, introduced in Ch. 2.)
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: A child's earliest vocabulary (~0;12 for speech, often ~0;8-0;9 in sign), similar across children; nouns for things and verbs for actions like 'cry' or 'eat'.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 11]

glossary.def: Blatantly and obviously failing to observe a maxim in order to trigger an implicature (the listener assumes cooperation and infers extra meaning) — e.g., sarcasm.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 8]

glossary.def: Someone who can readily use a language in conversation; fluent Elders and first-language speakers are central mentors in reclamation work.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 9]

glossary.def: A morpheme that can stand alone as a word (e.g., cat). Only roots can be free.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: A consonant with a narrow constriction causing turbulent, noisy airflow (frication) — e.g., the start of set and vet.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: A closed-class category providing grammatical 'glue' (determiner, auxiliary/tense, complementizer, pronoun, conjunction), as opposed to lexical categories.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: A synthetic type where a single affix fuses several grammatical meanings (e.g., Spanish -áramos = person+number+tense+aspect+mood).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: A framework (Chomsky & Halle 1968) in which URs are inputs 'generated' into SRs by ordered phonological rules; phonemes/rules may reflect cognitive reality.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 4]

glossary.def: A morpheme-by-morpheme translation line pairing each piece with its meaning/function, using abbreviations (1=first person, PL=plural, etc.).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: The opening between the vocal folds; the glottal place of articulation involves the vocal folds (e.g., the first sound of he/who).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: In linguistics, the mental system of knowledge underlying a language — not a book of 'proper-usage' rules. Every human language has a grammar.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: Whether a form could be generated by the mental grammar of a language. 'Ungrammatical' (marked with *) means the grammar cannot produce it — about what is possible, not merely what exists.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: In a matched-guise study, the varying label or presentation applied to the stimulus (e.g., the name on a résumé, an accent, a face shown with a voice).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: The static configuration of the base knuckles and interphalangeal joints (e.g., the ASL '5' or 'B' handshape); may be unmarked (common, basic) or marked.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: The central word of a phrase that determines its category and is obligatory; every phrase is a projection of a head (e.g., a noun heads an NP).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: Movement of a head into the next higher head position (e.g., T-to-C movement, which derives English yes-no questions).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: An experimental paradigm using an infant's sucking rate: a novel stimulus raises the rate; habituation lowers it; a change back up (dishabituation) shows the infant perceives a difference.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 11]

glossary.def: The one-word stage, where a single word conveys a whole utterance's worth of meaning.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 11]

glossary.def: A Coast Salish language of British Columbia, the focus of family- and community-based reclamation work described in the chapter.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 9]

glossary.def: The unique language variety of a single individual.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 10]

glossary.def: A multi-word expression whose meaning is non-compositional and must be stored as a whole (e.g., 'let the cat out of the bag').
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 7]

glossary.def: The meaning of an utterance in terms of what the speaker is doing with it (asserting, questioning, ordering) — the act performed in making the utterance.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 8]

glossary.def: A teaching setting where learners are surrounded by and use the target language (e.g., the Six Nations immersion program for Mohawk).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 9]

glossary.def: A clause type expressing a request or command (e.g., 'Open the door!').
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: A meaning a sentence suggests but does not necessarily make true; unlike an entailment, an implicature is cancellable (can be negated without contradiction).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 7]

glossary.def: Unconscious knowledge a fluent user has about their language that they cannot easily articulate (contrast: explicit knowledge).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: Replacing or mispronouncing someone's name to make it 'sound more English/white,' stripping their connection to family, community, and language (Bucholtz).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: The way linguistic forms point to social meaning. Referential indexicality points to something in context; non-referential indexicality signals social identity/stance.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 10]

glossary.def: In a ditransitive, the (often recipient) argument, frequently marked by 'to'; accusative in English (dative in languages with dative case).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: A predicate expressing a stable, more-or-less permanent property (e.g., 'is tall', 'is intelligent').
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 7]

glossary.def: An affix inserted inside another morpheme (e.g., Tagalog -um- in t-um-akbuh 'ran').
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: Morphology expressing grammatical information appropriate to a word's category; it never changes the category (e.g., -s plural, -ed past, agreement).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: A learner's own evolving language system, distinct from both the L1 and the target L2, with its own rule-governed patterns (Selinker 1972).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 12]

glossary.def: A morphological change that alters sounds inside a root rather than adding an affix (e.g., mouse→mice, sit→sat); irregular in modern English.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: A standard transcription system (est. 1886) with one symbol per phone; its underlying structure (like the periodic table) matters more than memorizing symbols.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: A clause type used to ask a question — either a yes-no question or a content (wh-) question.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: Pitch manipulated across phrases/sentences for conversational functions (e.g., statement vs. question). Such a language is intonational.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: A language where words tend to be morphologically simple, expressing grammar via separate function words (e.g., Mandarin, Cantonese; English is fairly analytic).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: A test using the frame 'It is/was ___ that ___'; only a constituent can go in the blank.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: The language of the Kanien'kehá:ka (Mohawk); an Iroquoian language discussed by Dr. David Kanatawakhon-Maracle (Turtle Clan Mohawk).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 9]

glossary.def: The principle, stressed by the chapter's contributors, that a language carries cultural knowledge and cannot be taught apart from its culture (e.g., Mohawk nyaweh means far more than English 'thank you').
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 9]

glossary.def: The mental process of perceiving and understanding linguistic input.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 13]

glossary.def: A typical developmental achievement reached around a certain age (babbling, first words, two-word stage, etc.).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 11]

glossary.def: Governmental/institutional rules that encourage or force the use (or non-use) of languages, require proficiency, or regulate languages in public space — usable to erase OR reinforce identities.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: The mental process of planning and generating linguistic output (speech or sign).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 13]

glossary.def: A community's work to reclaim and bring back use of its heritage language, especially after colonial suppression; the theme uniting this chapter (Mohawk, Michif, Hul'q'umi'num', Nishnaabemwin).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 9]

glossary.def: Efforts to restore vitality to an endangered or dormant language by growing its number of speakers and its everyday use.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 9]

glossary.def: The finding that a person's native language influences how they process linguistic input (e.g., which phonological contrasts the brain responds to).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 13]

glossary.def: A program trained on a vast corpus that calculates the probability that pieces of language relate to one another, used to generate statistically plausible text; it has no mind or communicative intent.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: The 'voice box' at the top of the trachea; a set of cartilages surrounding the airway, housing the vocal folds.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: The historical suppression of Indigenous languages (including through residential schools), which made speaking them feel shameful and drove language endangerment — the backdrop reclamation responds to.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 9]

glossary.def: A word's grammatical class (part of speech: noun, verb, adjective, adverb), defined by distribution (grammatical context), not meaning.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: The study of the meaning of individual words (the semantic information stored with a lexical item, alongside its form and syntactic category).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 7]

glossary.def: Stress whose placement is unpredictable and memorized per word; can create minimal pairs. Contrast with predictable (rule-governed) stress.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: Allomorph choice determined by the specific root, which must be memorized (e.g., ox→oxen, sheep→sheep).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: The 'killing' of a language through policy (e.g., residential-school prohibitions on Indigenous languages).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: Judgments people (including linguists) make about others based on how they use language.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: The meaning encoded by linguistic expressions themselves (words/sentences), as opposed to non-linguistic 'meaning' (e.g., 'those clouds mean rain').
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 7]

glossary.def: A point in a language where speakers have two or more ways of expressing the same thing in the same linguistic environment (e.g., the -ing variable: walking vs. walkin').
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 10]

glossary.def: The scientific study of human language: describing the patterns of languages and drawing conclusions about the shared systems in speakers' and signers' minds.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: Where in space or on the body a sign is articulated (default = neutral signing space in front of the torso).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: How air flows through the vocal tract, based on the size/shape of the constriction (stop, fricative, approximant, affricate, tap, trill).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: Rhythmic, syllable-like babbling on the hands by babies acquiring a signed language — evidence that babbling reflects the ambient language, not just random motor activity.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 11]

glossary.def: The modality of signed languages: articulated by the hands/arms (manual), transmitted by light waves (photic), received by sight (visual).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: A noun treated as an uncountable substance, taking 'much' and resisting plural/numerals (e.g., water, furniture).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 7]

glossary.def: A technique for revealing hidden attitudes: hold a STIMULUS constant and vary its GUISE; any difference in participant ratings is attributed to the guise, not the stimulus.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: A conversational maxim: be clear — avoid obscurity and ambiguity, be brief and orderly.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 8]

glossary.def: A conversational maxim: be truthful — do not say what you believe to be false or lack evidence for.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 8]

glossary.def: A conversational maxim: be as informative as required, but not more informative than needed.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 8]

glossary.def: A conversational maxim (relevance): make your contribution relevant to the conversation.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 8]

glossary.def: The shared cognitive system in a language user's mind that lets them produce and understand a language and be understood by others who know it.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: The part of the grammar that links forms (sounds, signs, or symbols) to meanings — a kind of dictionary in the mind.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: Conscious knowledge you have about your grammar, as distinct from the (often unconscious) grammatical knowledge itself.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: A distinct Indigenous people whose historically multilingual communities are associated with Michif and a homeland spread across the Prairies and northern US.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 9]

glossary.def: A mixed language of the Métis people combining Algonquian (e.g., Cree/Ojibwe/Saulteaux) and French elements; spoken across the western provinces and into North Dakota.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 9]

glossary.def: Two signs (or, in Ch.4, two words) that differ in exactly one parameter/property — e.g., ASL SORRY vs. PLEASE differ only in handshape.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: A language whose grammar and lexicon draw substantially from two source languages (Michif is a well-known example).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 9]

glossary.def: The physical channel of a language: whether it is vocalized (spoken) or signed.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: A vowel with a stable quality from start to finish.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: The smallest systematic pairing of form (sound/sign) and meaning or grammatical function (e.g., cat, -s, inter-).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: A word containing more than one morpheme (e.g., cats, non-renew-abil-ity); a one-morpheme word is morphologically simple.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: The part of grammar dealing with the meaningful pieces inside words and how they combine (e.g., adding -s to make a plural).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: How the manual articulators move: path movement (elbow/shoulder, moving through space) vs. local movement (wrist/radioulnar/knuckles).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: A sequence of N items occurring in a given order in a corpus (bigram = 2, trigram = 3), used to model co-occurrence probabilities.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: Whether a vowel is oral (raised velum) or nasal/nasalized (lowered velum, e.g., the vowel in bent).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: A set of phones that share phonetic properties AND share phonological behaviour; must be exhaustive for the language (e.g., English voiceless plosives [p t k]).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 4]

glossary.def: Two words that would be a minimal pair except for extra difference(s) elsewhere; weaker evidence, so several are needed.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 4]

glossary.def: A classical theory of word meaning: the minimal set of conditions that something must meet (necessary) and that suffice (sufficient) to belong to a category (e.g., defining 'doe').
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 7]

glossary.def: An expression (e.g., 'any', 'ever', 'lift a finger') that is only licensed in negative or similar downward-entailing environments.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 7]

glossary.def: When an existing-language feature differs from the target and interferes (a common source of L2 accent and errors).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 12]

glossary.def: The study of how the brain supports language, using brain measures (e.g., electrical activity/EEG) to test where and when linguistic processing happens.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 13]

glossary.def: Learning a language in an unfamiliar modality (e.g., a hearing speaker learning a signed language as an M2 learner), where learners transfer existing iconic gesture at first.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 12]

glossary.def: An Anishinaabe (Ojibwe) language variety; the chapter describes learning it in a university/community setting.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 9]

glossary.def: Meaning that is not part of the literal surface content (e.g., implicatures and presuppositions); not targeted by 'it is not the case that…'.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 8]

glossary.def: An invented word used for testing; speakers' acceptance of a nonce word can show two phones contrast without a real minimal pair.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 4]

glossary.def: Signing articulators other than the hands/arms — torso, head, face (brow, eyes, cheeks, lips) — which carry essential meaning.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: The loudest, most prominent core of a syllable, usually a vowel (or a syllabic consonant, e.g., the second syllable of bottle).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: The methodological problem that to study natural vernacular speech, linguists must observe it — but observation makes speech less natural.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 10]

glossary.def: The class of consonants with significant obstruction to airflow: oral stops, fricatives, and affricates.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: Social/psychological harm done to discourse participants (hearers/viewers) by an expression in a given context; can occur regardless of the speaker's intent.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: A predicate taking a single argument; its denotation is the set of things that satisfy it (⟦sour⟧ = the set of all sour things).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 7]

glossary.def: The consonant(s) before the nucleus. A margin (onset or coda) is simple with one phone, complex with two or more.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: The view that vocal language is more important than signed language — a bias that has caused harm to deaf people and to the study of sign languages.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: The direction the hand faces (palm orientation + finger orientation), set by the wrist, radioulnar, elbow, and shoulder joints.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: Using a word too broadly, applying it to things outside its adult meaning (e.g., calling anyone with a beard 'Dada', or a motorcycle by one's word for a car).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 11]

glossary.def: Applying a regular pattern to an irregular form (e.g., 'goed', 'foots') — evidence the child has learned the rule.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 11]

glossary.def: Prestige attached to a standardized, socially dominant variety, openly recognized as 'correct.'
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 10]

glossary.def: The four categories describing a sign: handshape, orientation, location, and movement.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: A derogatory term (jerk, idiot, asshole; also called a general pejorative) condemning a specific person for specific behavior, rather than an entire group.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: The target (upper) articulator a consonant moves toward — e.g., upper lip, teeth, alveolar ridge, palate, velum, uvula, pharyngeal wall.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: Improved comprehension of an unfamiliar talker or accent as a result of more listening experience; extends across speakers and even across different accents.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: The process by which infants, initially sensitive to many phonemic contrasts, tune to the contrasts of their ambient language(s) and lose sensitivity to unused ones.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 11]

glossary.def: The subfield studying how the body perceives and processes linguistic signals (works for both signed and spoken languages).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: An utterance that not only conveys information but performs an action that changes reality (e.g., 'I concede,' 'I now pronounce you married') — provided the right authority, sincerity, and audience uptake exist.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: The property of language by which utterances (and other social practices) can perform actions and affect reality, including constructing identity (Austin; extended by Butler).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: The general category of manipulating airflow with the vocal folds. In this book limited to voiced vs. voiceless.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: An individual unit of speech that can be part of a word in a language; what counts as a phone depends on whether the sound appears in ordinary words of that language.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: An abstract sound category that speakers treat as a single unit; notated in slashes / /. A phoneme is a set of allophones that appear in different environments (e.g., English /t/ = {[ɾ],[tʰ]…}).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 4]

glossary.def: The process of determining a language's phonemes, their allophones, and each allophone's distribution; the result is a phonemicization.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 4]

glossary.def: How much two phones share in articulation; used (with complementary distribution) to decide whether they're allophones of the same phoneme.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 4]

glossary.def: The area of grammar concerned with the physical production and perception of the sounds or signs of language.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: The process turning a UR into an SR by applying phonological rules; shown in a derivation table (UR on top, rules down the side, SR on the bottom; — = rule didn't apply).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 4]

glossary.def: A statement A → B / C _ D: a target natural class (A) changes (B) in a stated environment (C _ D). Notation uses → , / , _ (target position), and # (word boundary).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 4]

glossary.def: Allomorph choice determined by surrounding sounds (e.g., a/an; English plural [s]/[z]/[ɪz] by the final sound).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: The part of grammar governing how the physical units of a language can be combined and how they change in different contexts.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: Language-specific restrictions on which combinations of units are allowed in which positions (e.g., English bans [tl]/[dl] onsets).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 4]

glossary.def: A set of words that act together as a single unit and can occupy the same structural position.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: A rule (e.g., S → NP VP) specifying how a constituent breaks into smaller constituents; equivalent to a tree diagram.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: The auditory perception of vocal-fold vibration rate (the physical rate is the fundamental frequency, f0).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: The overall combination of an active and a passive articulator (e.g., bilabial, labiodental, alveolar, velar, glottal). Named active-first (e.g., labiodental).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: The most common oral stop: lung air trapped behind the closure, then released in an explosive burst (e.g., English p, t, k, b, d, g).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: When an existing-language feature matches the target and helps learning (e.g., the new language has a phoneme contrast the learner already has).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 12]

glossary.def: The part of grammar concerned with how meaning arises in context (e.g., how 'I have some news' can be read as good or bad).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: The state, event, or activity a sentence attributes to its subject (in this chapter, a single head — usually a verb or adjective — that combines with a subject and objects).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: An affix attached before its base (e.g., inter- in international).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: Prescribing how people should or should not use language (e.g., style-guide 'rules'). Not the goal of linguistics.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: The social value attached to a language variety; higher-prestige forms are often those used by more powerful or privileged groups, not objectively superior ones.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: A special kind of entailment that a sentence takes for granted / assumes to be true already (e.g., 'again' presupposes a prior occurrence).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 7]

glossary.def: The meaning of a complex expression is determined by the meanings of its parts AND how those parts are combined (not just which words, but their structure).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 7]

glossary.def: When two analyses fit the data equally, prefer the simpler one (fewest statements/rules).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 4]

glossary.def: Automatic, skill-like knowledge used without conscious effort (fluent real-time use); the other memory system relevant to language learning.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 12]

glossary.def: A rule that applies to EVERY form meeting its target and environment, with no exceptions (typical of spoken-language phonological rules; signed languages seem to lack these).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 4]

glossary.def: The property that a language can produce an infinite number of new words and sentences from a finite vocabulary and finite set of combining principles. Also called creativity.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: How well a learner can use the language; gaining proficiency means moving from limited toward more native-like comprehension and production.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 12]

glossary.def: A standardized scale for rating proficiency (e.g., ACTFL Proficiency Guidelines, the CEFR/Canadian Language Benchmarks), used by programs including language-reclamation schools.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 12]

glossary.def: The content of a declarative sentence that can be true or false.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 7]

glossary.def: A theory/observation that categories have fuzzy boundaries and better/worse examples; the 'cup or bowl' experiments show categorization isn't captured by strict necessary-and-sufficient conditions alone.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 7]

glossary.def: The study of the mental processes involved in language production and comprehension, using experiments (e.g., reaction times) to test theories of how linguistic knowledge is deployed in real time.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 13]

glossary.def: The idea that abstract linguistic units (like phonemes) are not just analysts' constructs but are actually used by the mind/brain — supported by psycho- and neurolinguistic evidence.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 13]

glossary.def: An illocutionary act of inviting the addressee to supply information.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 8]

glossary.def: Studying change by comparing a community's speech at two actual points in time.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 10]

glossary.def: Repurposing a slur as a marker of shared identity and solidarity against oppression (e.g., 'queer'); not all targeted members may be ready to embrace a reclaimed term.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: The property that a structure can contain another instance of the same kind of structure (e.g., a clause inside a clause), allowing infinitely long sentences.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: Repeating part or all of a word as a morphological process (e.g., Halq'eméylem qwélqwel 'talkative'; English 'salad-salad').
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: The actual thing in the world (or cognitive model) that a linguistic expression points to on a given use.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 7]

glossary.def: The smallest possible base — the indivisible core of a word (e.g., cat, library, nation).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: Lip shape in a vowel: rounded (boot) vs. unrounded (spread as in beat, or neutral as in but).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: Any language learned after one already has an L1 (even if it is one's third or fourth language). One's L2 accent is shaped by the phonology of one's L1.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: The study of how people learn an additional language after early childhood (SLA); this book frames it broadly to include later language learning of any kind, including reclamation contexts.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 12]

glossary.def: A head's requirement about what complement it combines with (e.g., a transitive verb selects an object).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: The part of grammar that calculates the meanings of words, phrases, and sentences; works together with syntax.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: The meaning of a word that language users store in their heads — the concept associated with the expression (e.g., what you know when you know the word strawberry).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 7]

glossary.def: A softer version of the critical-period idea: a span of heightened (but not strictly all-or-nothing) readiness for language learning.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 11]

glossary.def: A string of words expressing a complete statement, question, or command; a clause that stands on its own as an utterance. A statement expresses a proposition (true or false).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: The basic independent meaningful unit of a signed language (equivalent to a spoken word); analyzed by parameters rather than phones.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: A sentence with only one clause.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: An affix realized at the same time as its base — common in signed languages (added motion) and tone languages (tonal morphemes).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: Acquiring two (or more) languages from early childhood at the same time; children can separate the systems and reach native competence in each.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 11]

glossary.def: An insult that denigrates a specific marginalized group; targets a person BECAUSE of group membership. Power imbalance is essential — insults aimed at high-status groups lack the same force.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: A statistical association between a linguistic variable and a social factor such as class, gender, age, or ethnicity.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 10]

glossary.def: Variation within a single language/variety (and even within one speaker), as opposed to cross-linguistic variation between different languages.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 10]

glossary.def: The class of consonants with relatively free airflow: nasal stops, approximants, taps, and trills.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: An abstract measure of a phone's relative prominence (roughly loudness); a sonority hierarchy orders phones (vowels highest, obstruents lowest).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: The tendency for sonority to rise through the onset, peak at the nucleus, and fall through the coda (e.g., [plænt] obeys it; *[lpætn] violates it).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: Use of 'they/them' to refer to a single, known individual (e.g., 'Samnang told me they needed an extension'); an in-progress grammatical change resisted by prescriptivists.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: A phrase in a designated structural position at the top edge of a phrase (e.g., the subject is the specifier of TP).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: An act performed by producing an utterance (asserting, questioning, promising, pronouncing); performatives are one kind. Applies across modalities.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 8]

glossary.def: A predicate expressing a temporary state or stage (e.g., 'is available', 'is being restless right now').
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 7]

glossary.def: The variety of a language that most closely matches dictionaries, textbooks, and high-status media; its status comes from social/economic/political power, not from being linguistically 'better.'
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: Negative attitudes and expectations attached to a non-standard accent or variety (the variety itself is neither good nor bad); can cause real harm in jobs, housing, courts, and education.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: In a matched-guise study, the element held constant across conditions (e.g., the résumé, the sales script, the recorded voice).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: The first major sign-notation system (Stokoe 1960), which analyzed signs into parameters and showed signed languages have full linguistic structure.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: A consonant with complete closure blocking airflow. Oral stops (raised velum) include plosives, ejectives, implosives, clicks; nasal stops (lowered velum) send air through the nose.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: Extra prominence on a syllable (via loudness, duration, and/or pitch). Levels: primary [ˈ], secondary [ˌ], and unstressed.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: When one string of morphemes (or words) has more than one possible structure and therefore more than one meaning (e.g., unlockable).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: Varying one's speech across situations; in Labov's attention-paid-to-speech model, more careful speech goes with more attention (other motivations exist too).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 10]

glossary.def: The argument that (in English) appears before the predicate and controls verb agreement; nominative case if a pronoun (I, we, they).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: The English yes-no-question process that reverses subject and auxiliary (You have left → Have you left?); analyzed as T-to-C head movement.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: An affix attached after its base (e.g., -s in cats).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: An irregular pattern that replaces a morpheme's form entirely (go→went, good→better→best); always memorized, often on very frequent words. A type of allomorphy.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: The (relatively concrete) phonetic form of a word, made of phones, written in [ ]. Also called the phonetic representation.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 4]

glossary.def: Associating phones to positions in syllable structure, based partly on sonority.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: A layer of structure (abbreviated σ) between the word and the phone; every syllable has a nucleus and optional onset/coda.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: An ASL phonotactic constraint: a two-handed sign with both hands moving must use the same handshape and move the same way (rare exceptions exist).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 4]

glossary.def: A transformation that moves an element from its base position to another position in the tree (e.g., head movement, wh-movement); shown by striking the base position and drawing an arrow (trace notation is an alternative).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: The part of grammar that determines how words can and cannot be combined into phrases and sentences.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: A language with much word-internal morphology; subtypes are agglutinative and fusional.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: A word or expression whose use is avoided except in certain circumstances; using it in the wrong context breaks the taboo and causes offence. Taboos can arise for negative OR positive (respect) reasons.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: A strategy of replacing a taboo word with another word — either to avoid resembling it (e.g., Kambaata in-law names) or to evoke it via a similar form (e.g., 'sugar,' 'shoot' for a swear).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: An early multiword stage containing mostly content words (nouns, verbs) and omitting function words like obligatory determiners — like a telegram.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 11]

glossary.def: Tongue-root position distinguishing tense (advanced root, e.g., beat) from lax (retracted root, e.g., bit) vowels.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: The role a participant plays in an event (agent, experiencer, theme/patient, instrument, goal, source, etc.); also called theta role.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: The thematic role of a participant that something happens to; a patient is a theme that is also changed by the event.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: An organizing history: 1st wave correlates variables with broad social categories; 2nd wave adds locally meaningful community facts; 3rd wave treats variation as active identity/style construction.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 10]

glossary.def: In an LLM, a unit of language — a letter, word, piece of a word (morpheme), or punctuation mark — whose co-occurrence probabilities are calculated.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

glossary.def: Pitch manipulated at the syllable/word level to change meaning (high/low/mid). A language using it is a tone/tonal language.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: The effect of a person's existing knowledge (e.g., of words) on how they perceive incoming input — knowledge shaping perception.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 13]

glossary.def: The especially offensive emotional power of slurs, arising from the power differential and the invocation of historical violence against the targeted group; so strong that even mentioning some slurs can cause harm.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: The X-bar analysis of a sentence: a projection of T (tense/auxiliary), with the subject in its specifier and the VP as its complement. (Also called IP.)
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: Notating the phones of a word unambiguously; can be broad (minimal detail) or narrow (fine detail). Written in square brackets [ ].
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: The influence of a learner's existing language(s) on the new one.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 12]

glossary.def: The number of arguments a predicate takes (also called valency): intransitive (1: subject), transitive (2: subject + object), ditransitive (3: subject + two objects).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: A vowel phone that moves through three qualities (e.g., Vietnamese rượu 'alcohol').
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: The conditions under which a sentence would be true; at-issue (literal) meaning is often called truth-conditional meaning.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 7]

glossary.def: Using a word too narrowly, applying it to fewer things than the adult meaning covers.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 11]

glossary.def: The abstract phonemic form of a word, made of phonemes, written in / /. Also called the phonemic representation; the input to a derivation.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 4]

glossary.def: The difference between USING a word to refer to something in the world vs. MENTIONING the word itself as a linguistic object (conventionally shown in italics).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: One of the alternative forms of a linguistic variable (e.g., [ɪŋ] vs. [ɪn] for -ing).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 10]

glossary.def: The study of language variation and change that counts and quantifies variants of linguistic variables to uncover social patterns; grew out of dialectology (Labov).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 10]

glossary.def: A neutral term for any subdivision of a language (used in this chapter to avoid the loaded connotations of 'dialect').
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 10]

glossary.def: The natural, everyday way a person uses language when not monitoring their speech (e.g., when not being recorded by a linguist).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 10]

glossary.def: Quietly failing to observe a maxim (e.g., lying), without intending the listener to derive an implicature — unlike flouting.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 8]

glossary.def: Two membranes in the larynx that can vibrate; the space between them is the glottis.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: A voice quality produced by very low-frequency vocal-fold vibration, sounding creaky; a normal part of many languages' phonetics/prosody, disproportionately criticized in women's voices.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: The lips, tongue, and other parts of the mouth and throat used to articulate spoken language, often shown in a midsagittal diagram.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: The modality of spoken languages: articulated with the vocal tract (vocal), transmitted by sound waves (acoustic), received by hearing (auditory).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: Vocal-fold vibration. A phone with vibration is voiced (e.g., buzz's [z]); one without is voiceless/unvoiced (e.g., bus's [s]).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: A phone made with a wider opening than a consonant; described by quality (height, backness, rounding) rather than place/manner.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: Vertical tongue position: high (beat), mid (bet), or low (bat).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: Duration contrast between long and short vowels (phonemic in Japanese; sub-phonemic in English). Long/short consonants = geminates/singletons.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: The overall configuration of tongue and lips in a vowel; more of a continuum than consonant categories.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 3]

glossary.def: An expression involving taboo bodily references (e.g., shit, ass).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 2]

glossary.def: A sign process where the nondominant hand is dropped entirely (a kind of deletion) in a two-handed sign.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 4]

glossary.def: A sign process where the moving nondominant ('weak') hand stops moving in a two-handed sign.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 4]

glossary.def: Movement of a wh-phrase to the front of the clause (into the specifier of CP) to form a content question.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: The smallest separable unit of language — the smallest unit that can stand on its own in an utterance and move independently in a sentence.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

glossary.def: The order of words in a sentence; fixed in some languages (English) and flexible in others (Latin, Kanien'kéha, ASL), where order is often set by topic/focus.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: A method (Berko 1958) using nonce words like 'wug' to show children apply morphological rules productively (one wug, two wugs).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 11]

glossary.def: A theory constraining tree structure: every phrase (XP) is the projection of a head (X) through an intermediate bar level (X'), with positions for a specifier, complement(s), and adjuncts.
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 6]

glossary.def: A morpheme with no overt form, written ∅ (e.g., the plural of sheep/deer).
glossary.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 5]

flashcards.back: The scientific (descriptive, empirical) study of human language and the shared mental systems behind it.
flashcards.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

flashcards.back: The shared system in users' minds that lets them understand and be understood — not prescriptive 'rules.'
flashcards.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

flashcards.front: Name the components of mental grammar.
flashcards.back: Phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, pragmatics (plus the mental lexicon).
flashcards.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

flashcards.back: Descriptive = describe what users actually do; prescriptive = dictate what they 'should' do. Linguistics is descriptive.
flashcards.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

flashcards.back: An ungrammatical form — one the mental grammar cannot generate (e.g., *'lbitfer').
flashcards.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

flashcards.back: Arbitrariness — the pairing is conventional, not inherent (with some iconic exceptions).
flashcards.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

flashcards.back: A finite vocabulary + finite rules can generate infinitely many new words and sentences.
flashcards.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

flashcards.back: Whether it is vocalized (spoken) or signed.
flashcards.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

flashcards.front: Is reading/writing part of core mental grammar?
flashcards.back: No — it's a secondary skill; users have full grammars without literacy, and some languages have no written form.
flashcards.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

flashcards.back: Conscious knowledge about your grammar, vs. the unconscious grammatical knowledge itself.
flashcards.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

flashcards.front: Three accessible tools of language science?
flashcards.back: Acceptability judgments, surveys, and corpora (plus experiments, phonetic software, neuroimaging).
flashcards.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

flashcards.back: By combining tokens in statistically probable sequences from training data — combinatorial, with no meaning or intent of its own.
flashcards.source: [Anderson et al. (2022), Essentials of Linguistics, 2nd ed., Ch. 1]

flashcards.front: Human language vs. LLM output — key difference?
